name: Vinilogy Covers
author: vinilogy

sections.description:
Many independent record shops have hundreds or thousands of records online without a cover, or with the same placeholder image on every product. Vinilogy Covers finds those products, looks each record up in the Vinilogy catalogue and downloads its cover from Cover Art Archive.

It needs a free Vinilogy key, which you get with one click from the plugin screen, and it talks to the services listed under “External services”.

Nothing changes in your shop until you say so:

  • Covers are downloaded to your media library and wait for your review.
  • Each proposal shows the album found, why it was matched and a confidence score.
  • Approve them one by one, the ones you select, or all above a confidence level.
  • Anything you approve can be undone; discarded downloads are deleted.

How records are identified, from most to least reliable:

  1. Barcode (EAN/UPC), read from the usual barcode fields or from the SKU when it is a valid barcode: the cover of that very edition.
  2. Artist and title, read from product attributes or from the product name. Shop habits such as “SURNAME, NAME”, “(LP, 180g)”, “– COLOURED VINYL” or used-condition notes in the name (“VG+”) are cleaned up before searching.

It learns how your shop is organised. Every shop keeps its data its own way: the artist in a custom field of the theme, singles written “Side A/Side B”, the country at the end of the title… The first time, the plugin sends a small sample of your products without a cover to Vinilogy, which works out where your shop keeps the artist, the title and the barcode, and checks it against the catalogue. The plugin only uses that “recipe” if it finds more covers than the standard way, and the Settings show how your products are being read.

Proposals with a confidence of 85 or more come pre-selected. In our test with 100 records from one shop, every pre-selected proposal was correct; always review the rest.

Optional Discogs fallback. When Cover Art Archive has no image, the plugin can also use the Discogs cover from the Vinilogy catalogue. It is off by default: Discogs images are uploaded by its users and its terms restrict reusing them on other sites, so each shop decides. Every downloaded image records its source.

Vinilogy is a free comparison site for vinyl records sold by independent shops in Spain: https://www.vinilogy.com

External services

This plugin relies on external services to find and download covers. It only contacts them after a shop administrator clicks “Find products without a cover”, and then for each product in the queue (in the background, or while the Covers screen is open).

Vinilogy cover lookup – https://api.vinilogy.com (run by Vinilogy, https://www.vinilogy.com)
Used to identify each record and get the address of its cover.
Sent for each product without a cover: its barcode if it has one, otherwise the artist and title read from the product, plus the shop’s Vinilogy key. No data about customers, orders or users is sent.
Terms: https://www.vinilogy.com/condiciones#portadas – Privacy: https://www.vinilogy.com/privacidad#portadas

Vinilogy key request – https://api.vinilogy.com (run by Vinilogy)
Used once, only when you click “Get my free key”, to create your shop’s key and save it in the plugin.
Sent: the site name, the site address and the admin email. Vinilogy then requests one address of your site (/?rest_route=/vinicov/v1/reto) to check that the site is yours; that address shows a random code for a few minutes and nothing else. No data about customers, orders or users is sent.
Terms and privacy of Vinilogy: as above.

Vinilogy shop reading – https://api.vinilogy.com (run by Vinilogy)
Used to work out where the shop keeps the artist, the title and the barcode. Contacted the first time covers are searched, then about once a month, when “Read my products again” is clicked, or when almost no covers are being found.
Sent: a sample of up to 40 products without a cover, with their name, SKU, barcode field, attributes, categories, tags and short custom fields (never fields about prices, costs, stock or suppliers), plus the shop’s Vinilogy key. No data about customers, orders or users is sent.
Vinilogy may pass part of that sample to Claude, the AI of Anthropic, to read it. Anthropic: https://www.anthropic.com – Terms: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms – Privacy: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
Terms and privacy of Vinilogy: as above.

Cover Art Archive (run by the MetaBrainz Foundation and the Internet Archive) – https://coverartarchive.org
The cover image is downloaded from coverartarchive.org, which redirects to the Internet Archive (archive.org). The request carries the usual connection data (IP address of your server, user agent).
Terms: https://musicbrainz.org/doc/About/Data_License and https://archive.org/about/terms.php – Privacy: https://metabrainz.org/privacy and https://archive.org/about/terms.php

Discogs (only if the shop turns on the fallback) – https://www.discogs.com
The cover image is downloaded from i.discogs.com. The request carries the usual connection data.
Terms: https://support.discogs.com/hc/en-us/articles/360009334593-API-Terms-of-Use – Privacy: https://support.discogs.com/hc/en-us/articles/360009334513-Privacy-Policy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin (WooCommerce must be active).
  2. Open WooCommerce → Album covers and click “Get my free key”. The key is saved by itself.
  3. Click “Find products without a cover” and review the proposals.
sections.faq:
Will it change my products without asking?

No. Covers are only downloaded to the media library; a product changes only when you approve its cover, and you can undo it.

What counts as “without a cover”?

Products with no image, and products whose image is shared by many products (5 or more by default, adjustable), which is what a placeholder looks like. Products that already have their own cover are never touched, and if you set one by hand while a proposal is waiting, the proposal is dropped.

Does it cost anything?

No. The key is free and the plugin is free. Record shops are who Vinilogy is for.

How do I get a key? Do I need to email you?

No. Click “Get my free key” on the Album covers screen: Vinilogy checks that the site is yours by visiting it once, and the key is saved by itself. One key per site; asking again replaces the old key.

If your site cannot be reached from the internet (it runs on your own computer, is behind a password or in maintenance mode, or blocks the WordPress REST API), get the key by email instead: open https://api.vinilogy.com/tiendas/alta, enter your shop name, website and email, open the link we send you (it expires after 24 hours) and paste the key in Settings, at the bottom of the screen.

Versions before 0.2.3 told you to ask for a key by email. If your Album covers screen still says so, update the plugin.

I have thousands of records. How long does it take, and is there a limit?

There is no limit on the number of products. The Vinilogy service allows up to 120 lookups a minute for each key, and the plugin keeps to it by itself: if the service says “too many requests”, the plugin waits ten minutes and carries on where it stopped. You do not need to split your catalogue or do anything else.

How fast it goes depends on how it runs:

  • In the background (WordPress scheduled tasks): one batch a minute, up to 10 products per batch. That is at most about 600 products an hour, so 4,000 records take at least 7 hours. WordPress only runs scheduled tasks when someone visits the site, so a quiet site goes slower.
  • With the Album covers screen open, or with wp vinicov procesar: batches run one after another, without waiting a minute between them, so it is faster.

For a large catalogue we recommend:

  1. Run wp vinicov buscar and then wp vinicov procesar with WP-CLI if your host has it. Use --max=<n> to try a few hundred first, and wp vinicov estado to see where it stands.
  2. Review the proposals as they arrive; you do not have to wait for the whole catalogue. Approve those at 85 or more with wp vinicov ok --confianza=85 or on the screen, and look at the rest one by one.
  3. Use “Search again” for products marked “Not found” after fixing their names or adding barcodes.

How do I get the best matches?

  • Fill in the barcode (EAN/UPC) wherever you have it, in a barcode field or as the SKU. It finds the cover of that exact edition.
  • Without a barcode, the product needs the artist and the title: in product attributes (Artist / Title, Artista / Título, Album…) or in the product name, for example “Artist – Title (LP)”.
  • Format, colour and condition notes in the name (“180g”, “COLOURED VINYL”, “VG+”) are fine: they are cleaned up before searching.
  • If your shop keeps the artist somewhere else (a custom field of your theme, for example), you do not need to change anything: the plugin works it out from a sample of your products. See “How does it know where my shop keeps the artist?”.

How does it know where my shop keeps the artist?

The first time covers are searched, the plugin sends Vinilogy a sample of up to 40 of your products without a cover (see “External services”). Vinilogy looks for the field that holds artist names it knows, the field with real barcodes, and habits such as singles written “Side A/Side B” or a country at the end of the title. Then it searches some of those products both ways, and only gives your shop that recipe if it finds more covers than the standard way.

The Settings, under “How your products are read”, say where the artist, the title and the barcode are taken from and how the check went. It is checked again about once a month, on its own if almost no covers are being found, or when you click “Read my products again”. When the way of reading changes, products marked “Not found” go back to the queue.

Where do the covers go before I approve them?

To your media library, attached to the product but not used as its image. If you discard a proposal, that file is deleted.

What does the confidence number mean?

How sure the match is, from 0 to 100. Hover over it to see why: a barcode match of the exact edition scores highest; a match by artist and title scores lower when several albums or artists share that name. Proposals at 85 or more come pre-selected.

What if a cover is wrong?

Discard it, or undo it after approving: the product goes back to the image it had. You can always set your own image in the product editor, as usual.

Does it work with variable products?

It sets the cover of the parent product, like any other product. Variations keep their own images.

My SKUs are not barcodes. Does it still work?

Yes: the record is then identified by artist and title. A SKU is only treated as a barcode when it is a valid EAN/UPC (8, 12, 13 or 14 digits with a correct check digit).

The search does not advance when I close the page

Covers are fetched in the background by WordPress scheduled tasks. If your host has them disabled (DISABLE_WP_CRON), keep the Album covers screen open until the search finishes, or run wp vinicov procesar.

A product says “Not found”. What now?

Either Vinilogy does not have that record, or it has no cover image. Check that the product name has the artist and the title, or add a barcode, and use “Search again” at the bottom of the screen.

Who owns the covers?

Their labels and artists. Record shops use them to show the album they sell. Cover Art Archive collects them for that kind of use; check its terms and, if you turn on the Discogs fallback, Discogs’ terms.

What happens when I delete the plugin?

Its settings, queue and pending downloads are removed. Covers you already approved stay on your products; each image keeps a note of where it came from (Cover Art Archive or Discogs) in its custom fields, so you can find and remove them later if you ever need to.

Does it work from the command line?

Yes, with WP-CLI: wp vinicov buscar (queue products without a cover), wp vinicov procesar [--max=<n>] (fetch covers, optionally stopping after n products), wp vinicov ok --confianza=85 (approve all with that confidence or more), wp vinicov estado (counts by state and how your products are read), wp vinicov receta (check again how your products are read).

How do I report a security issue?

Write to hola@vinilogy.com. Please do not open a public issue.
sections.changelog:
0.2.6

  • New: get your free key with one click, from the plugin screen. Vinilogy checks that the site is yours by visiting it once and the key is saved by itself: no email, no copying and pasting. The web page with the emailed link is still there for sites that cannot be reached from the internet.

0.2.5

  • New: the plugin learns how your shop keeps its data. From a sample of products without a cover, Vinilogy works out where the artist, the title and the barcode are (a custom field of the theme, “Artist – Title” in the name, singles written “Side A/Side B”, a country at the end of the title…), checks it against the catalogue and only uses it if it finds more covers. Shown in Settings, under “How your products are read”, with a button to read them again.
  • New: after updating the plugin, or when the way of reading changes, products marked “Not found” go back to the queue on their own.
  • Fix: a barcode field is now only used when it holds a real barcode (correct check digit), as the SKU already was. Before, a catalogue number with 8 to 14 digits in it was sent as a barcode and nothing was found.
  • New WP-CLI command: wp vinicov receta (check how your products are read); wp vinicov estado shows it too.

0.2.4

  • Fix: when the artist comes from a product attribute and the product name is only the title (“HYAENA”), the whole name is now used as the title. Before, the title stayed empty and those products were never looked up.
  • Fix: a “:” or “-” inside the title (“La storia: parte 1”) no longer cuts the title when the artist is already known.

0.2.3

  • Free keys are now issued automatically at https://api.vinilogy.com/tiendas/alta (before, by email).

0.2.2

  • Spanish (es_ES) translation now ships with the plugin, so it shows in Spanish right after installing.

0.2.1

  • Longer prefix on all internal names, as requested by the WordPress.org plugin review.
  • Translations now come from translate.wordpress.org.
  • Clearer wording: approve, discard, undo. Messages say what happened to the products.
  • Never overwrites a cover you set by hand while a proposal was waiting; undo only restores if the image is still the approved one.
  • Pauses for ten minutes when the Vinilogy service cannot be reached, instead of retrying every minute.
  • A SKU only counts as a barcode when it is a valid EAN/UPC. Artist attributes with commas are no longer cut.
  • Duplicating or deleting a product no longer leaves cover data or files behind.
  • Each batch stops after 20 seconds and carries on in the next one.

0.2.0

  • Translatable (English base).
  • Discogs fallback, off by default.
  • Clean uninstall.
  • Declared compatible with WooCommerce order storage and block checkout.

0.1.0

  • First version, tested with 100 records of a real shop.

short_description: Finds the missing album covers of your WooCommerce record shop and sets them only after you approve them.
